novelty_verdict.hopkins_satellite_test: DONE BEFORE (general). Jiang et al. 2022 tested Hopkins with satellite phenology along an altitudinal gradient in SW China; Richardson 2019 used PhenoCam. Our novelty rests on the single-escarpment scale + thermal-belt twist + AlphaEarth angle, NOT on 'testing Hopkins from satellite' per se.
novelty_verdict.coldair_drainage_phenology_from_satellit: APPEARS NOVEL (strongest claim). Cold-air pooling's effect on forest COMPOSITION is documented (Kemppinen et al.), and cold-air pools are detectable in satellite LST, but no paper maps a thermal-belt inversion in satellite-derived spring GREEN-UP timing.
novelty_verdict.alphaearth_unsupervised_forest_gradient: PARTIALLY DONE. AlphaEarth clustering exists (urban/wetland); embeddings shown to encode elevation/temperature (R2~0.97). But unsupervised recovery of a xeric-ridge->mesic-cove forest-community moisture gradient looks novel.

comparison_numbers.jiang_2022_china: growing-SEASON-LENGTH shortens 15.2-25 days per km elevation (not SOS; not apples-to-apples with our 4.3 d/100m SOS lapse)
comparison_numbers.fu_2018_EPS: elevation-phenology-shift weakened ~34 d/1000m (1960s) -> ~22 d/1000m (now) under differential warming; our ~43 d/1000m is on the HIGH end and the literature predicts it should be weakening
comparison_numbers.kemppinen_coldair_inversion: 0.5-1.7 C per 100 m inversion strength, up to 16.2 C across a transect (New England, ground iButtons) -> magnitude to compare our MODIS night-LST result against
comparison_numbers.lei_smokies_cove_ridge: 14-18 day leaf-out difference between xeric ridge and mesic cove (ground) -> validates our aspect/moisture-gradient phenology twist
